ratchet_note: The frozen set was rebuilt twice as the simulated measurement and then the loss shapes changed (p1 mean → p1 sample → p2 with ramped losses); every rung is re-scored here on the latest set, p2. r6 had the best simulated score but made inertia on the dev events worse (MdAPE 15 → 20 %), so the release is r5.
verdict: Verdict. On inertia GridPulse beats the constant guess (16.4 % vs 20.4 %) but not a simple demand-scaling rule fitted on the four dev events (15.1 %); without the demand input the trace alone gives 20.3 %, no better than the constant. It overestimates 2023-2025 inertia by about 30 % (it learned the 2018-2022 inertia per MW of demand). MW lost is marginally better than the RoCoF formula on medium labels (25.9 % vs 27.1 %) but its error bars are too narrow (48 % inside 1σ). The early-warning forecasts only help at 5 s; by 10 s, simply holding the lowest value seen beats the nadir forecast, and holding the current value beats the 60 s forecast. On ERCOT the sim-trained summary model reads MW lost from the reported drop better than ERCOT's own MW/Hz constant (15.7 % vs 20.1 %), most clearly in 2023-2025, while GridSim's forward drop forecast is 29 % too deep on the exam years.
how: GridSim (Phase 1) solves the aggregated swing equation with per-technology governors (deadband, lag, rate limit, headroom, reheat / CCGT / hydro lead-lags), load damping, fast frequency response and under-frequency load shedding. Checked by Phase 1 against closed forms (RoCoF to 4e-14, nadir to 0.03 mHz) and ANDES (nadir 24 mHz off on a 200 MW step). GridPulse wraps generate_states: each random fleet is rescaled to a real GB or ERCOT operating point and given that grid's services. Initial RoCoF of the rescaled states matches ΔP·f0/2E to 0.1 %.

GB demand, inertia and wind/solar share are drawn together from NESO half-hours of the training-input years 2018, 2020 and 2022 (70 %) or from wide ranges (30 %). ERCOT load comes from EIA-930 in the same years, inertia ≈ 5 s × load. Losses 150-2,000 MW (GB) and 250-2,800 MW (ERCOT). GB response: governors 300-1,500 MW plus, in 60 % of states, Dynamic Containment built from NESO's service curve (nothing until 0.2 Hz, all of it at 0.5 Hz), Moderation and Regulation. ERCOT: load resources tripping at 59.7 Hz, FFR at 59.85 Hz, battery droop in half the states.

Prior-predictive twins of the 4 GB dev events (each event's own NESO inertia, demand and loss, everything else drawn): with generic services the real nadirs sat at the 2-6th percentile (the sims were too shallow); trimming 2019-era response put them at the 13-20th. ERCOT twins were 8-29 % too shallow with Phase 1's effective damping of 2.5 %/%; 1.0 %/% fits these random states. The 3 Dec 2019 dev label (1,788 MW) was replaced by Elexon metered output (854 MW) after the twins confirmed it was about twice too large. A dev check of the first-second drop favoured instantaneous 1 s samples over 1 s means, but the rung trained that way was not better.

Every simulated trip is sampled at 1 s with a random sub-second phase and added to a real quiet 140 s slice of NESO 1 s frequency (56,000 slices from 2018-07, 2020-07, 2022-01, at least 1 h from any event), then cut with the same onset rule griddata used on the real events and kept only if it would have been detected (≥0.15 Hz fall in 10 s for GB; ERCOT report criteria). A 0.44 M-parameter MLP with Gaussian heads reads the window −20…+60 s, masked after N s, plus the grid flag and demand. 28,201 detected events from 48,000 simulated states. ERCOT has no public traces, so a separate small sim-trained model reads its reported summary numbers.
limits: Inertia mostly comes from demand, not from the trace. Trace-only inertia error is 20 %, the same as guessing 230 GVA·s. One-second data blur the first-second RoCoF, and response arrives within 1-2 s, so the slope that carries inertia is barely sampled.
It learned 2018-2022 GB. In 2023-2025 inertia per MW of demand fell (NESO median 160-189 GVA·s); GridPulse still reads 216-244, so its exam-year error is 20-31 %.

Error bars are too narrow on real MW lost (48 % of medium-label events inside 1σ, 79 % inside 2σ) and slightly narrow on inertia (63 % / 89 %). Four dev events are too few to widen them properly. Nadir and 60 s bands are about right (60-75 % / 87-95 %).

The 60 s forecast is worse than holding the current value. Real GB frequency 30-60 s after a trip is shaped by secondary response, market actions and the next disturbance; GridSim models secondary control as a single ramp (Phase 1 limit 6).

ERCOT exam years are stiffer than GridSim. Forward drop forecasts are 29 % too deep (2023-2025 have gigawatts of battery FFR and ECRS). No ERCOT 1 s data exist, so the lab's ERCOT noise is scaled GB noise.
MW/Hz, headroom and FFR are weakly identifiable (sim skill 0.5-0.7 for MW/Hz, about 0.5 for headroom and FFR) and have no real truth to grade them on.
Not every detected GB event is a trip: some are fast demand or interconnector ramps; GridPulse reads them as trips. Loss labels themselves are noisy (REMIT timing, capacity vs output).
